title: Glimmer - Overnight rescue & transient runbook (scratch)
content:
Quick context (notes to self):
- This is a compact rescue checklist to use when the main runbook is too slow or the cluster is flapping. Keep it fast, reversible, and annotated.
- Intended for temporary fixes during overnight shifts or short escalations; document any steps you run here and file tidy follow-ups in PRODINF-842.

When I sign in:
- Check Slack #prod-incidents: last 2 threads, any pinned messages.
- Pager history: `ops pager logs 24h --service=inference` (or look at Incident log in Ops dashboard).
- Quick health dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/observability/summary (focus: 90th latency, error rate, GPU utilization)

Immediate triage matrix (if traffic is degrading or errors rising):
1) Scope: isolate whether error is widespread or a small subset (model/client/region).
   - Query: `SELECT region, model, count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 10` (dashboard shortcut)
   - If only one model: try model variant fallback (see "fallbacks").
2) Latency spike with CPU/GPU saturation:
   - Check nodes: `bastion> for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu -o name); do ssh $n nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv; done`
   - If GPU mem pressure: consider moving heavy batches to burst pool or enable lighter quantized variant.
3) High error rate, 503s or 504s:
   - Check inference-runtime logs: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/inference-api --since=15m --tail=200`
   - Search for OOM, KV cache errors, or kernel mismatches.

Fast, reversible actions (use only if safe):
- Temp route: set routing policy to prefer small-model variants (5–15 minutes)
  - Command (console quick patch): go to Console > Routes > edit route for /generate > set fallback weight: small-quantized-v2:80, base-v1:20. Note: document change in incident thread.
- Reduce batch size globally (short window): edit config map `runtime-config.batch.max_tokens=512` then rollout with `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-api`
- Clear per-customer prefix cache (if cache corruption suspected): `redis-cli -h cache-prod.lcl del prefix:customer:1234:*` (be conservative).
- If a single node is flapping: cordon it and drain: `kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`. Watch metrics for sudden spike.

Escalation/contact quick list:
- Primary SRE oncall: Arjun Patel (Slack @arjun, phone XXX-555-0121)
- Infra engineering lead: Lina Moreno (Slack @lina, call if persistent config bug)
- Product PM (if customer-visible regression): Samir Qureshi (add to incident: @samir)
- Security: security-oncall@redwood.com (if data exposure suspected)

Rollback / follow-up tasks (always add to the ticket):
- If you touched routing or config: revert after 30 mins of stability and record observed metrics (pre/post).
- Create a short runbook entry with exact commands used and times. Tag as "temporary-fix".
- File a postmortem if customer impact > 5% error rate for > 15 minutes.

Useful command snippets (copyable):
- Get top erroring models: `curl -s "https://metrics-api.local/query?expr=topk(10,sum(rate(requests{status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (model))" | jq .`
- Restart inference service: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-api`
- Check GPU memory on suspected pod host: `ssh gpu-host-23 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv`

Notes-to-self / things to add after shift:
- Add a Console quick action for model-fallback weights so we don't edit route JSON during pager noise.
- Demo the "reduce batch" knob in next runbook review (it saved 20% tokens during last incident).
- Investigate why KV cache mismatches happen under spike (link to shard map in PRODINF-842).

Open questions / unknowns (put in PRODINF-842):
- Are there automated safeguards for routing changes (can we TTL them automatically)?
- How to get faster visibility into which customer prefixes are affected (add sample-level tracing?).

Sticky log entries (examples I keep copying):
- "Kernel mismatch error: failed to load fused_op for int8 path" -> try fallback build `runtime:quant-light` and tag incident.
- "KVCacheEvict: inconsistent-prefix" -> run cache inspection script: `scripts/inspect-cache.sh --prefix=...`

Afterhand checklist for incoming shift:
- Copy the incident summary into next person’s note and slack the key action items (changes made, why, how to revert).
- Leave a single-line status at top of ticket: e.g., `STATUS: transient routing applied -> stable at 2025-11-05 03:22 UTC; fallback weight=80% small-quantized-v2`
- Confirm nobody else is actively rolling other infra changes (check #deployments).

Micropersonalities (my quick heuristics):
- If CPU is normal and GPU is pegged, suspect attention-kernel/quantization fallback.
- If errors spike only in eu-west, suspect network egress or region routing policy.

End of quick scratch.

PRIORITY: If you touch anything irreversible, call Lina first.

(leave a timestamped note here after any action)
- 2025-11-05 02:03 UTC: lowered routing weight; saw error rate drop from 6.2% -> 1.1% in 11m.
- 2025-11-05 02:28 UTC: drained gpu-node-17; no regressions observed.

-- Maya T.
